observation_basis: Visual statements are supplied by the root device operator. This analysis reads only the immutable saved prefix. Screenshot paths below are journal references; their ongoing files were not read. Retained raw screenshot payload hashes are verified separately.
save_interpretation: Both offline starts confirm save_bytes=36/save_sequence=1 from the earlier linked exits. The changed CLOCK setting was visible before Back. No SAVE_WORKER_STOP or CARTRIDGE_STOP follows this A launch before the panic/reboot, so successful save2 completion or CLOCK persistence cannot be inferred. B has not exited in this prefix. In the later prefix, B visibly returns CLOCK to ON before Back, then also panics/reboots without a successful save/cartridge stop. Visible restoration before exit is not persistent restoration.
pending: A CLOCK persistence and restoration after reboot/relaunch
Remediate and physically retest both save-task crashes

prior_failures_retained: The sealed linked record retains native cadence about28.6/28.8FPS below the30FPS release floor and lifetime audio underruns. This follow-up supplies no new cadence qualification.

crash_attribution.direct_evidence: Stack protection fault explicitly names task game_save on Core1; reported SP is4bytes below its lower bound. AUDIO_WORKER_STOP precedes the panic and is not the failing-task identity.
crash_attribution.decoded_root_cause: A named panic PC/RA symbolize to cross-core critical-section entry during flash/NVS; address-shaped stack words include read_legacy_registry and platform_save_seal_object_is_allowed. These are candidate stack symbols, not an unwound call chain. Explicit game_save task and stack-bound violation support save-task stack exhaustion. B independently reports the same task/fault type; no B full unwind or successful NVS commit is claimed.
